$comment: Generated from varnish-common/schema/values.schema.yaml by generate.py. Do not edit.
description:
Values are validated against values.schema.json when you run helm install,
upgrade, template or lint. Unknown keys and values of the wrong type are
rejected, and the error names the offending path, for example
`at '/server': additional properties 'foo' not allowed`. Pass
`--skip-schema-validation` to skip this check; the checks done by the chart
templates still apply.

nameOverride.description:
Overrides the name of the chart (without the release name). For example, setting `nameOverride` to "hello" would produce a workload named "release-name-hello". Containers within a pod derive their name from this setting.

By default, the name of the chart is used.

fullnameOverride.description: Overrides the full name of the chart (with the release name). This setting allows overriding both the release name and the workload name altogether. For example, setting `fullnameOverride` to "hello" would produce a workload named "hello".

imagePullSecrets.description: An array of objects that conforms to the Kubernetes [imagePullSecrets][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition. When set, each item in an array must consist of an object with a key `name` referencing the Kubernetes secret.

initContainer.description: Overrides the default busybox initContainer image.

image.description: The image to use for the initContainer.

tag.description: The tag to use for the initContainer image.

podSecurityContext.description:
An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [securityContext][k8s-pod-v1-pods] definition of a Pod.

This securityContext will be set on all Pods within this chart. For setting securityContext on all containers, see `global.securityContext`.

securityContext.description:
An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [securityContext][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container.

This securityContext will be set on all containers within this chart. For setting securityContext on the Pod itself, see `global.podSecurityContext`.

annotations.description:
Applies extra annotations to all workloads. The value can be set as either an object or a template string. Workload annotations can be used for applying additional metadata or for integrating with external tooling. The annotations specified here will be applied to the workload itself.

To apply annotations on a Pod, use `global.podAnnotations`. To apply annotations on a specific workload, use `server.annotations`.

podAnnotations.description:
Applies extra annotations to all Pods. The value can be set as either an object or a template string. Pod annotations can be used for applying additional metadata or for integrating with external tooling. Annotations specified here will be applied to a Pod itself.

To apply annotations on a workload, use `global.annotations`. To apply annotations on a specific Pod, use `server.podAnnotations`.

labels.description:
Applies extra labels to all workloads. The value can be set as either an object or a template string. Workload labels can be used for applying additional metadata or for integrating with external tooling. The labels specified here will be applied to the workload itself.

To apply labels on a Pod, use `global.podLabels`. To apply labels on a specific workload, use `server.labels`.

podLabels.description:
Applies extra labels to all Pods. The value can be set as either an object or a template string. Pod labels can be used for applying additional metadata or for integrating with external tooling. Labels specified here will be applied to a Pod itself.

To apply labels on a workload, use `global.labels`. To apply labels on a specific Pod, use `server.podLabels`.

resources.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes resources definition of a Container. This configuration will apply resource constraints to all containers. To specify resources on a single container, use `server.resources`, `server.varnishncsa.resources`, and `server.otel.resources`.

natsServer.description: An object configuring Varnish Controller Agent access to NATS.

externalAddress.description: An FQDN to the NATS server. The value is ignored if `global.natsServer.internal.enabled` is set to true. Required when `server.agent.enabled` is set to true and `global.natsServer.internal.enabled` is set to false.

enabled.description: Configures Varnish Agent to use the internal NATS server. `"-"`, the Varnish Controller Helm Chart default for this shared global value, is treated as `true`.

namespace.description: Discovers the internal NATS server within the given namespace. By default, the current namespace is used.

releaseName.description: Overrides the full name of the internal NATS server. Required if `nameOverride` or `fullnameOverride` is used in the Varnish Controller Helm Chart. By default, "varnish-controller" is used.

passwordFrom.description:
Sets internal NATS password from an external secret. Internal NATS must be configured separately. See [Varnish Controller Helm Chart documentation](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-helm/varnish-controller/configurations/) for more information.

Note: if internal Varnish Controller is deployed on another namespace than the one Varnish Enterprise is deployed to, the `varnish-controller-credentials` secret needs to be manually copied from the Varnish Controller namespace.

name.description: The name of the secret holding the internal NATS password.

key.description: The key of the secret holding the internal NATS password.

clusterDomain.description: Overrides the Kubernetes cluster domain. Required if Kubernetes cluster is configured to use different cluster domain than the default. By default, "cluster.local" is used. In most cases, this value should not be changed.

create.description: Create a Kubernetes service account to use with the workload.

labels.description: Applies extra labels to the service account. The value can be set as either an object or a template string.

annotations.description: Applies extra annotations to the service account. The value can be set as either an object or a template string.

name.description: Overrides the name of the service account. By default, the full name of the chart is used when `serviceAccount.create` is `true`, and `default` otherwise.

replicas.description:
Specifies the number of replicas to deploy Varnish Enterprise server. The value is ignored if `server.kind` is "DaemonSet".

When `server.autoscaling.enabled` is set to `true`, and `server.autoscaling.minReplicas` is `-`, the value of `server.replicas` will be used. `server.replicas` is ignored if `server.autoscaling.minReplicas` is set to a number.

kind.description: Specifies the type of workload to deploy Varnish Enterprise server. The value can be one of `Deployment`, `DaemonSet`, or `StatefulSet` depending on usage scenarios.

labels.description: Applies extra labels to the workload. The value can be set as either an object or a template string. Labels specified here will be applied to the workload itself. To apply labels on the Pod, use `server.podLabels`.

licenseSecret.description: Sets the secret for using a varnish-enterprise.lic file. See [Varnish Enterprise installation](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-helm/varnish-enterprise/installation/).

annotations.description: Applies extra annotations to the workload. The value can be set as either an object or a template string. Workload annotations can be used for applying additional metadata or for integrating with external tooling. The annotations specified here will be applied to the workload itself. To apply annotations on the Pod, use `server.podAnnotations`.

strategy.description: Configures [deployment strategy][k8s-deployment-strategy] to replace existing Pod with a new one. This configuration is only available when `server.kind` is set to Deployment. For StatefulSet and DaemonSet, see `server.updateStrategy`.

updateStrategy.description:
Configures update strategy for updating Pods when a change is made to the manifest. This configuration is only available when `server.kind` is set to StatefulSet or DaemonSet. For Deployment, see `server.strategy`.

*Note: While both StatefulSet and DaemonSet share the same `updateStrategy` configuration key, its applicable values are different. See [updateStrategy on StatefulSet][k8s-statefulset-updatestrategy] and [updateStrategy on DaemonSet][k8s-daemonset-updatestrategy].*

hostNetwork.description:
Whether to enable hostNetwork for the Varnish Enterprise Pod. This will make the Varnish Enterprise Pod bind to the port of the host instead of using a container network provided by Kubernetes.

Setting this will also set the DNS policy to `ClusterFirstWithHostNet` to allow the Pod to communicate with Kubernetes DNS.

shareProcessNamespace.description: Whether to enable shared PID namespace between all containers in a Pod. This is useful for a scenario where it is necessary to send a signal to a process across a container.

workDir.description: Sets the Varnish working directory (the `-n` argument of varnishd), relative to `/var/lib/varnish`. When set to "-", the Pod name is used. When empty, varnishd runs without `-n` and uses the Varnish default, so `varnishstat`, `varnishadm` and `varnishlog` work without `-n` in `kubectl exec` and in extra containers.

enabled.description: Configures Varnish to listen for HTTP traffic.

port.description: Configures the TCP port on which Varnish will listen for HTTP traffic. This port is used for Varnish to bind to within a container. To change the port exposed via service to other applications, see `server.service.http.port`.

address.description: Configures the address on which Varnish will listen for HTTP traffic. Ignored when `server.http.podIP` is `true`.

podIP.description: Configures Varnish to listen for HTTP traffic on the Pod IP address instead of `server.http.address`. Note that this makes port forwarding with kubectl harder.

hostPort.description: Sets the port to expose HTTP traffic directly on the node the Pod runs on, as the container's [hostPort][k8s-pod-v1-containers].

enabled.description: Configures Varnish to listen for HTTPS traffic using native TLS. When enabled, `server.tls.config` should also be set. Certificates may be mounted into the Pod using `server.extraVolumeMounts` and `server.extraVolumes`.

port.description:
Configures the TCP port on which Varnish will listen for HTTPS traffic. This port is used for Varnish to bind to within a container. To change the port exposed via service to other applications, see `server.service.https.port`.

This port is used by the HTTPS service as a targetPort.

hostPort.description: Sets the port to expose HTTPS traffic directly on the node the Pod runs on, as the container's [hostPort][k8s-pod-v1-containers].

address.description: Configures the address on which Varnish will listen for HTTPS traffic. Only applicable when neither `server.tls.config` nor `server.tls.configFile` is set.

config.description: The TLS configuration, passed to varnishd with `-A`. It is recommended to reference the port with the `{{ .Values.server.tls.port }}` template string to keep the configuration in sync with the service.

configFile.description: Uses the content of the given file as `server.tls.config`. The file is parsed as a template string and must be placed inside the `files/` directory of the Helm chart. Overrides `server.tls.config` if set.

address.description: Configures the address for Varnish management interface.

port.description: Configures the port for Varnish management interface.

extraListens.description: An array of extra ports for Varnish to listen to.

name.description: The name of the listen. This name will be accessible in VCLs via `local.socket`.

proto.description: The protocol of the listen. Must be one of `PROXY` or `HTTP`. Default to HTTP if not set.

port.description: The port to listen to. Required unless `server.extraListens[].path` is set. Only applicable for TCP listens.

address.description: The address to listen to. Only applicable for TCP listens.

hostPort.description: The port to expose this listen directly on the node the Pod runs on, as the container's [hostPort][k8s-pod-v1-containers]. Only applicable for TCP listens.

path.description: The path of the UNIX domain socket to listen to. Required unless `server.extraListens[].port` is set. Only applicable for UNIX domain sockets.

user.description: The user owning the UNIX domain socket. Only applicable for UNIX domain sockets.

group.description: The group owning the UNIX domain socket. Only applicable for UNIX domain sockets.

mode.description: The file mode octet for the UNIX domain socket, as a quoted string (e.g. "0700"). Only applicable for UNIX domain sockets.

extraEnvs.description: Sets additional environment variables for the Varnish Enterprise container. The value can be set as an object, an array of objects, or a template string.

ttl.description: Sets the default Time To Live (in seconds) for a cached object.

minThreads.description: Sets the minimum number of worker threads in each pool. See also [varnishd documentation][varnishd].

maxThreads.description: Sets the maximum number of worker threads in each pool. See also [varnishd documentation][varnishd].

threadTimeout.description: Sets the number of seconds after which idle threads are destroyed.

command.description: Sets the command for Varnish Enterprise. Note that by overriding this, you will also override parameters, listening ports, etc. See also [varnishd documentation][varnishd].

extraArgs.description: Sets the extra arguments to varnishd. A string is split on whitespace into separate arguments, while each item of a list is passed as a single argument, so use a list for values containing spaces.

parameters.description: Sets Varnish Enterprise parameters (the `-p` argument of varnishd). Parameter names are converted from camelCase to snake_case, and arrays are joined with a comma.

extraInitContainers.description: An array of objects that conform to the Kubernetes [initContainers][k8s-pod-v1-pods] definition of a Pod. This can be used to run initialization tasks before varnishd starts. Note that `initContainers` cannot be changed once it is applied. To update this value after the initial deploy, uninstall Varnish Enterprise Helm Chart from the cluster and reinstall. The value can be set as either an array of objects or a template string.
examples:
- name: varnish-setup-tls
  securityContext:
    {{- toYaml .Values.global.securityContext | nindent 4 }}
  image: debian:latest
  command:
    - sh -c "sleep 3600"

extraContainers.description: An array of objects that conforms to the Kubernetes [containers][k8s-pod-v1-pods] definition of a Pod. This can be used to add a sidecar container to varnishd. The value can be set as either an array of objects or a template string.
examples:
- name: varnish-hello
  securityContext:
    {{- toYaml .Values.global.securityContext | nindent 4 }}
  image: hello-world:latest
  volumeMounts:
    - name: {{ .Release.Name }}-varnish-vsm
      mountPath: /var/lib/varnish

extraVolumeClaimTemplates.description: An array of objects that conforms to the Kubernetes [VolumeClaimTemplates][k8s-volume-claim-templates] definition of a StatefulSet workload. This configuration is only available when `server.kind` is set to StatefulSet.
examples:
- metadata:
    name: {{ .Release.Name }}-pv
  spec:
    accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
    resources:
      requests:
        storage: "10G"

extraVolumeMounts.description: An array of objects that conforms to the Kubernetes [volumeMounts][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. This configuration is used to mount extra volumes defined in `server.extraVolumes` into the Varnish Enterprise container. The value can be set as either an array of objects or a template string.

extraVolumes.description: An array of objects that conforms to the Kubernetes [volumes][k8s-pod-v1-pods] definition of a Pod. This configuration is used to define volumes to be used in `server.extraVolumeMounts`, or within `server.extraContainers`, or within `server.extraInitContainers`. The value can be set as either an array of objects or a template string.

mse.description: An object for configuring the Massive Storage Engine (MSE).

enabled.description:
Enables Massive Storage Engine. Only one of `server.mse.enabled` or `server.mse4.enabled` must be enabled.

When set to a string "-", `server.mse.enabled` will be set to an opposite value of `server.mse4.enabled` (i.e. automatically disabling MSE when MSE4 is enabled, and vice versa).

memoryTarget.description: Sets the amount of memory to use for MSE. The value can be set as either a percentage (e.g., "80%"), or bytes ("512m"). If cgroups resource limits are used (i.e., `server.resources`), the percentage is calculated from the resource limit that is assigned to the container.

config.description:
An MSE configuration. By default, the value is unset and MSE is run in a [memory-only mode](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-enterprise/features/mse_4/#getting-started-with-ephemeral-caching). See also the examples in [MSE Quick Start](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-enterprise/features/mse_4/#getting-started-with-persisted-caching-in-mse4) for more information on how to configure MSE.

If `server.mse.persistence.enabled` is true, it is recommended to reference to MSE path using `{{ .Values.server.mse.persistence.mountPath }}` template string in the configuration.

configFile.description: Use the content of the given file path as MSE configuration. The file will be parsed as templated string. Will override `server.mse.config` if set. Note that the file must be placed inside the files/ directory in the Helm chart itself.

enabled.description: Enables MSE persistence mode using [PersistentVolumes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/). This configuration is only available when `server.kind` is set to StatefulSet. See the [using StatefulSet](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-helm/varnish-enterprise/deployments/statefulset/) documentation for more information.

bookSize.description:
Database size relative to `server.mse.persistence.storageSize`, for auto-configuring MSE. Can be set as a percentage or a value.

`server.mse.persistence.bookSize` and `server.mse.persistence.storeSize` must add up to 100% or `server.mse.persistence.storageSize`. Only applicable if `server.mse.config` is empty.

storeSize.description: Sets the store size for MSE store. Can be set as a percentage (e.g. `1%`) or a literal size (e.g. `10Gi`). When the value is set as a percentage, the value will be relative to `server.mse.persistence.storageSize`.

mountPath.description: Sets the mount path for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE.

labels.description: Sets the extra labels for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE. Can be set as an object or a template string.

annotations.description: Sets the extra annotations for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE. Can be set as an object or a template string.

accessModes.description: Sets the storage access modes for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE.

storageClassName.description: Sets the storage class for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE.

storageSize.description: Sets the storage size for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE.

mse4.description: An object for configuring the Massive Storage Engine 4 (MSE4).

enabled.description: Enables Massive Storage Engine 4. Only one of `server.mse.enabled` or `server.mse4.enabled` must be enabled.

memoryTarget.description: Sets the amount of memory to use for MSE4. The value can be set as either a percentage (e.g., "80%"), or bytes ("512m"). If cgroups resource limits are used (i.e., `server.resources`), the percentage is calculated from the resource limit that is assigned to the container.

config.description:
An MSE4 configuration. By default, the value is unset and MSE4 is run in a memory-only mode.

If `server.mse4.persistence.enabled` is true, it is recommended to reference to MSE path using `{{ .Values.server.mse4.persistence.mountPath }}` template string in the configuration.

configFile.description: Use the content of the given file path as MSE4 configuration. The file will be parsed as templated string. Will override `server.mse4.config` if set. Note that the file must be placed inside the files/ directory in the Helm chart itself.

enabled.description: Enables MSE4 persistence; only applicable if `server.kind` is `StatefulSet`. Note that the backing storage must be "ext4".

bookSize.description:
Database size relative to `server.mse4.persistence.storageSize`, for auto-configuring MSE4. Can be set as a percentage or a value.

`server.mse4.persistence.bookSize` and `server.mse4.persistence.storeSize` must add up to 100% or `server.mse4.persistence.storageSize`. Only applicable if `server.mse4.config` is empty.

storeSize.description:
Store size relative to `server.mse4.persistence.storageSize`, for auto-configuring MSE4. Can be set as a percentage or a value.

`server.mse4.persistence.bookSize` and `server.mse4.persistence.storeSize` must add up to 100% or `server.mse4.persistence.storageSize`. Only applicable if `server.mse4.config` is empty.

mountPath.description: Sets the mount path for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE4.

labels.description: Sets the extra labels for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE4. Can be set as an object or a template string.

annotations.description: Sets the extra annotations for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE4. Can be set as an object or a template string.

accessModes.description: Sets the storage access modes for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE4.

storageClassName.description: Sets the storage class for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE4.

storageSize.description: Sets the storage size for the PersistentVolumeClaim for MSE4.

secret.description: Sets the Varnish secret for accessing the varnishd admin interface. Either this value or `server.secretFrom` can be set. If unset, Varnish will generate one on every Pod start.

secretFrom.description: Sets the Varnish secret from an external Kubernetes secret for accessing the varnishd admin interface. Either this value or `server.secret` can be set.

name.description: The name of the Kubernetes secret. Required when `server.secretFrom` is set.

key.description: The key of the Kubernetes secret holding the Varnish secret. Required when `server.secretFrom` is set.

secretFile.description: Use the content of the given file path as Varnish secret. The file will be parsed as templated string. Will override `server.secret` if set. Note that the file must be placed inside the files/ directory in the Helm chart itself.

vclConfigPath.description: A path to the main VCL configuration. This configuration affects the location where `server.vclConfig` will be saved to, as well as the `VARNISH_VCL_CONF` environment variable in the Varnish Enterprise container.

vclConfig.description: A VCL configuration for Varnish Enterprise.

vclConfigFile.description: Use the content of the given file path as VCL configuration. The file will be parsed as templated string. Will override `server.vclConfig` if set. Note that the file must be placed inside the files/ directory in the Helm chart itself.

vclConfigs.description:
Extra VCL configuration where a filename as a key and template string as a value. The path to store `server.vclConfigs` will be relative to that of `server.vclConfigPath`.

If the filename in `server.vclConfigs` matches the name in `server.vclConfigPath`, it will be treated in the same way as `server.vclConfig`. In this case, `server.vclConfig` must not be set.

vcls.description: Per-domain VCL routing (multi-tenant). When `server.vcls.routes` is set, the chart generates a routing VCL and a cmdfile from these settings, superseding the `server.vclConfig*` fields. `server.cmdfileConfig` and `server.cmdfileConfigFile` must not be set when `server.vcls.routes` is non-empty.

routes.description: Per-domain VCL routing. When set, the chart generates a routing VCL and a cmdfile that load each route as a separate VCL and select it based on the Host header, superseding `server.vclConfig`, `server.vclConfigFile`, `server.vclConfigs` and `server.cmdfileConfig` (which must not be set). Each route must set `vclContent`, and can set `name` (defaults to the first hostname, prefixed with `route_` if it does not start with a letter) and `hostnames`. As it is used as a VCL label, `name` must start with a letter. A route without hostnames is a catch-all and must be the last one.

name.description: The name of the route, used as a VCL label, so it must start with a letter. Defaults to the first hostname, prefixed with `route_` if it does not start with a letter, or to `any` for a route without hostnames.

hostnames.description: The hostnames to match for this route. A route without hostnames is a catch-all and must be the last one.

vclContent.description: The VCL of the route. Required.

includes.description: Shared VCL files placed in `/etc/varnish/vcls/`, next to the route VCLs. Each key is a filename and each value a template string. Requires `server.vcls.routes`. Route VCLs include them with a relative path (`include "./helpers.vcl";`), as plain filenames are looked up in `vcl_path` instead.

cmdfileConfigPath.description: A path to the [CLI command file][varnish-cmdfile]. This configuration affects the location where `server.cmdfileConfig` will be saved to, as well as the `-I` argument in the Varnish Enterprise container when `server.cmdfileConfig` is not empty.

cmdfileConfig.description: A [CLI command file][varnish-cmdfile] for running management commands when `varnishd` is launched. For example, when loading extra VCL in multi-tenancy mode. See also [External VCL ConfigMap](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-helm/guides/using-external-vcl-configmap/#configmap-for-multiple-vcl-files).
examples:
vcl.load vcl_tenant1 /etc/varnish/tenant1.vcl
vcl.label label_tenant1 vcl_tenant1
vcl.load vcl_main /etc/varnish/main.vcl
vcl.use vcl_main

cmdfileConfigFile.description: Use the content of the given file path as a cmdfile. The file will be parsed as templated string. Will override `server.cmdfileConfig` if set. Note that the file must be placed inside the files/ directory in the Helm chart itself.

baseUrl.description: Sets a base URL for Varnish Controller and Varnish Controller Router when performing a HTTP-based routing. If unset, the URL will infer from a Pod IP and `server.http.port`.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description:
Sets the termination grace period seconds to wait for Varnish Enterprise to shut down. Once this number of seconds is reached without the Varnish Enterprise Pod shutting down, Kubernetes will send SIGKILL to the Pod. When `server.delayedShutdown` is used, this value should be set to a higher value than the **maximum** time (in seconds) it took for Varnish Enterprise to fully shut down after a delayed shutdown.

The value to set here depends on the cluster setup. For example, an AWS Load Balancer may still forward requests to Varnish for `deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds` which is set to 300 seconds by default. If `server.delayedShutdown` took 30 seconds, then `server.terminationGracePeriodSeconds` should be set to _at least_ 330 seconds in order to have a zero-downtime during a rolling update or scaling down.

delayedHaltSeconds.description: Delays stopping of the Varnish Enterprise container by the given seconds.

delayedShutdown.description: Configures delayed shutdown for zero-downtime downscaling.

method.description:
Sets the method for delaying the shutdown of Varnish Enterprise. This is useful for rolling updates or when scaling down, where the load balancer component may still attempt to forward requests to the Varnish Enterprise instance when Varnish Enterprise has already received a SIGHUP, leading to HTTP 502 errors.

Multiple methods are provided here:

- `sleep` will simply sleep in the `preStop` for `server.delayedShutdown.sleep.seconds` seconds. This is the simplest way to delay the shutdown of Varnish Enterprise when the time taken for the load balancer component to stop forwarding traffic to Varnish Enterprise is largely fixed.
- `mempool` polls varnishstat for `MEMPOOL.sess` to go down to zero. This allows for the quickest shutdown but requires tuning `server.delayedShutdown.mempool.pollSeconds` to traffic patterns (as `MEMPOOL.sess` may become 0 momentarily, resulting in an early shutdown).

When `server.delayedShutdown.method` is set to a value other than "none", `server.terminationGracePeriodSeconds` **must** also be set.

seconds.description: Sets the number of seconds to sleep before SIGHUP is sent to Varnish Enterprise. Only applicable when `server.delayedShutdown.method` is set to "sleep".

pollSeconds.description:
Sets the number of seconds to poll for `MEMPOOL.sess` stats. Only applicable when `server.delayedShutdown.method` is set to "mempool".

This value requires tuning to traffic patterns. If the time between each traffic took more than `server.delayedShutdown.mempool.pollSeconds`, then Varnish Enterprise could be signaled to SIGHUP too early, leading to an HTTP 502 error on the load balancer (as Varnish Enterprise already stopped accepting connection).

waitSeconds.description: Sets the number of seconds to wait after `MEMPOOL.sess` turned zero. Only applicable when `server.delayedShutdown.method` is set to "mempool".

shutdownDelay.description: Configures the "shutdown_delay" delayed shutdown method. It is similar to `sleep`, but uses the `shutdown_delay` feature of Varnish Enterprise (6.0.13r2 and newer) to perform the wait in-engine instead of relying on `preStop` and an external command.

seconds.description: Sets the number of seconds to delay the shutdown in-engine. Only applicable when `server.delayedShutdown.method` is set to "shutdown_delay".

image.description: Sets the image and tag to use to deploy Varnish Enterprise.

repository.description: Sets the repository for Varnish Enterprise image.

pullPolicy.description: Sets the [imagePullPolicy][k8s-pod-v1-containers] for the Varnish Enterprise image. This can be one of Always, Never, or IfNotPresent.

tag.description: Sets the tag for the Varnish Enterprise image. By default, this is set to the same application version as in the Varnish Enterprise Helm Chart. If the tag is set to non-exact versions (such as "latest"), make sure to set `server.image.pullPolicy` to "Always" to make sure the image is always updated.

enabled.description: Enables the [HorizontalPodAutoscaling][k8s-hpa] with the Varnish Enterprise Pod. `server.replicas` is ignored if autoscaling is enabled.

minReplicas.description: Sets the minimum number of replicas to always keep running. When set to "-", the value of `server.replicas` is used.

maxReplicas.description: Sets the maximum number of replicas to run at most.

behavior.description: Sets the [HorizontalPodAutoscaling][k8s-hpa] behavior. The value can be set as either an object or a template string.

metrics.description: Sets the [HorizontalPodAutoscaling][k8s-hpa] metrics. The value can be set as either an array or a template string.
examples:
- type: Resource
  resource:
    name: cpu
    targetAverageUtilization: 80

pdb.description: An object for configuring [PodDisruptionBudget][k8s-pdb]. See also [Specifying a Disruption Budget for your Application](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/configure-pdb/).

enabled.description: Enables PodDisruptionBudget.

minAvailable.description: Sets the number or percentage of pods that must be available after the eviction. Required if `server.pdb.enabled` is true and `server.pdb.maxUnavailable` is not set.

maxUnavailable.description: Sets the number or percentage of pods that can be unavailable after the eviction. Required if `server.pdb.enabled` is true and `server.pdb.minAvailable` is not set.

enabled.description: Enables the [Service][k8s-service] for Varnish Enterprise.

labels.description: Applies extra labels to the Service. The value can be set as either an object or a template string.

annotations.description: Applies extra annotations to the Service. The value can be set as either an object or a template string.

type.description:
Sets the type of the Service. Can be either `ClusterIP`, `LoadBalancer`, or `NodePort`.

See also [Accessing Varnish Enterprise in Kubernetes Cluster](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-helm/guides/accessing-varnish-enterprise/).

clusterIP.description:
Sets a custom [Service ClusterIP][k8s-service-clusterip]. This value can be set as either an IP address, or a literal string "None". Only applicable when `server.service.type` is set to ClusterIP. When set to "None", Kubernetes will create a Headless Service, skipping the Kubernetes proxying mechanism. In such case, `server.service.http.port` and `server.service.https.port` are ignored, and `server.http.port` and `server.tls.port` are used instead.

See also [Accessing Varnish Enterprise in Kubernetes Cluster](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-helm/guides/accessing-varnish-enterprise/).

loadBalancerIP.description: Sets a pre-allocated IP address for use in LoadBalancer.

http.description: Enables or disables the Varnish HTTP service.

enabled.description: Enables HTTP service. Requires `server.http.enabled`.

port.description: Sets the port to expose HTTP service.

nodePort.description:
Sets the port to expose HTTP service directly on the node itself. Only applicable when `server.service.type` is set to NodePort. This value must be within the Kubernetes service-node-port-range (default: 30000-32767).

See also [Accessing Varnish Enterprise in Kubernetes Cluster](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-helm/guides/accessing-varnish-enterprise/).

https.description: Enables or disables the Varnish HTTPS service.

enabled.description: Enables HTTPS service. Requires `server.tls.enabled`.

port.description: Sets the port to expose HTTPS service.

nodePort.description:
Sets the port to expose HTTPS service directly on the node itself. Only applicable when `server.service.type` is set to NodePort. This value must be within the Kubernetes service-node-port-range (default: 30000-32767).

See also [accessing Varnish via NodePort](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-helm/guides/accessing-varnish-enterprise/#nodeport).

extraServices.description: An array of extra services to expose via the Service. Each extra service adds a port named `extra-<name>` to the Service.

name.description: Sets the name of the extra service. Required.

targetPort.description: Sets the port in the Pod to forward requests to, as a number or as a port name such as `extra-<name>` for `server.extraListens`. It must also be defined in `server.extraListens`. Required.

port.description: Sets the port to expose this extra service. Required unless the Service is headless (`server.service.clusterIP` set to "None"), in which case `targetPort` is used instead.

nodePort.description: Sets the port to expose this extra service on the node itself. Only applicable when `server.service.type` is set to NodePort. This value must be within the Kubernetes service-node-port-range (default: 30000-32767).

internalTrafficPolicy.description: Sets the internal traffic policy for this service. InternalTrafficPolicy describes how nodes distribute service traffic they receive on the ClusterIP. Can be set to `Local` or `Cluster`. If unset, the Kubernetes default (`Cluster`) is used.

externalTrafficPolicy.description: Sets the external traffic policy for this service. externalTrafficPolicy describes how nodes distribute service traffic they receive on one of the Service's "externally-facing" addresses (NodePorts, ExternalIPs, and LoadBalancer IPs). Can be set to `Local` or `Cluster`.

enabled.description: Enables the [Ingress][k8s-ingress] for Varnish Enterprise. Requires `server.service.http.enabled` and `server.service.http.port`.

labels.description: Applies extra labels to the Ingress. The value can be set as either an object or a template string.

annotations.description: Applies extra annotations to the Ingress. The value can be set as either an object or a template string.

ingressClassName.description: Sets the [Ingress Class][k8s-ingress-class] for selecting Ingress controller to use.

pathType.description: Sets the [Ingress Path Type][k8s-ingress-path-type] for the Varnish Enterprise endpoint. The value can be either `Prefix`, `Exact`, or `ImplementationSpecific`. The value to use here depends on the Ingress controller.

hosts.description: Sets the hostnames for the Ingress. These hostnames are used for routing traffic.

host.description: Sets the hostname to route traffic for.

paths.description: Sets the paths to route to Varnish Enterprise for this host, as an array of strings. Defaults to `/` when empty.

tls.description: An array of objects that conforms to [Ingress TLS][k8s-ingress-tls].

podAnnotations.description: Applies extra annotations to the Pod. The value can be set as either an object or a template string. Pod annotations can be used for applying additional metadata or for integrating with external tooling. Annotations specified here will be applied to the Pod. To apply annotations on the workload, use `server.annotations`.

podLabels.description: Applies extra labels to the Pod. The value can be set as either an object or a template string. Labels specified here will be applied to the Pod itself. To apply labels on the workload, use `server.labels`.

securityContext.description:
An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [securityContext][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container.

This securityContext will be set on the Varnish Enterprise container. For setting securityContext on the Pod itself, see `global.podSecurityContext`. For setting securityContext to all containers, see `global.securityContext`.

startupProbe.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [startupProbe][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container.

readinessProbe.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [readinessProbe][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. Set to `false` to disable the probe.

httpGet.description:
Uses Kubernetes [httpGet probe][k8s-probes] instead of TCP probe. Port will be automatically injected. It is possible to provide extra configuration options that conforms to the Kubernetes httpGet probe definition.

See also `server.startupProbe.httpGet`.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Sets the initial delay before the first probe is sent to determine if the Varnish Enterprise Pod is ready to accept an incoming connection.

periodSeconds.description: Sets the delay between each probe to determine if the Varnish Enterprise Pod is ready to accept an incoming connection after the initial probe.

timeoutSeconds.description: Sets the timeout for the probe to wait for a response from the Varnish Enterprise Pod.

successThreshold.description: Sets the number of times when a consecutive successful response is considered a success and the Varnish Enterprise Pod is considered ready to accept an incoming connection.

failureThreshold.description: Sets the number of times when a consecutive failure response is considered a failure and the Varnish Enterprise Pod is considered unhealthy.

livenessProbe.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [livenessProbe][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. Set to `false` to disable the probe.

httpGet.description:
Uses Kubernetes [httpGet probe][k8s-probes] instead of TCP probe. Port will be automatically injected. It is possible to provide extra configuration options that conforms to the Kubernetes httpGet probe definition.

See also `server.startupProbe.httpGet`.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Sets the initial delay before the first probe is sent to determine if the Varnish Enterprise Pod is still ready to accept an incoming connection (i.e., live).

periodSeconds.description: Sets the delay between each probe to determine if the Varnish Enterprise Pod is still ready to accept an incoming connection after the initial probe.

timeoutSeconds.description: Sets the timeout for the probe to wait for a response from the Varnish Enterprise Pod.

successThreshold.description: Sets the number of times when a consecutive successful response is considered a success and the Varnish Enterprise Pod is considered still ready to accept an incoming connection.

failureThreshold.description: Sets the number of times when a consecutive failure response is considered a failure and the Varnish Enterprise Pod is considered unhealthy (i.e., down).

resources.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [resources][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. This configuration can be used to limit resources consumed by the Varnish Enterprise container.

nodeSelector.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [nodeSelector][k8s-pod-v1-pods] definition of a Pod. This configuration is used to select a node to schedule a Pod to. The value can be set as either an object or a template string.

tolerations.description: An array of objects that conforms to the Kubernetes [tolerations][k8s-pod-v1-pods] definition of a Pod. This configuration is used to allow the Pod to be scheduled to nodes with specific taints. The value can be set as either an array of objects or a template string.

affinity.default:
podAntiAffinity:
  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - labelSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ include "varnish-common.name" . }}
          app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
      topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
affinity.description: This configuration is used to fine-grain control the scheduling of the Pod. By default, this is set to ensure all Varnish Enterprise Pods are always run in a different node. To disable this behavior, set to empty string ("") or `false`. The value can be set as either an object or a template string.

networkPolicy.description: An object for configuring the [NetworkPolicy][k8s-networkpolicy] of the Varnish Enterprise Pods.

enabled.description: Enables the NetworkPolicy.

allowIngress.description: Allows all connections from any source. Set to false when using `server.networkPolicy.extraIngress`.

allowEgress.description: Allows all connections to any destination. Set to false when using `server.networkPolicy.extraEgress`.

extraIngress.description: An array of ingress rules that conforms to the Kubernetes [NetworkPolicyIngressRule][k8s-networkpolicy-v1] definition. Only used when `server.networkPolicy.allowIngress` is false.

extraEgress.description: An array of egress rules that conforms to the Kubernetes [NetworkPolicyEgressRule][k8s-networkpolicy-v1] definition. Only used when `server.networkPolicy.allowEgress` is false.

enabled.description: Enables HTTP request logging via [varnishncsa][varnishncsa].

image.description: Sets the image and tag to use to deploy the varnishncsa sidecar. Setting a field to "-" inherits it from `server.image`.

repository.description: Sets the repository for Varnish Enterprise image for use with varnishncsa. The Varnish image used here must be the same version as the Varnish Enterprise server. Set this to "-" to inherit the value of `server.image.repository`.

pullPolicy.description: Sets the [imagePullPolicy][k8s-pod-v1-containers] for the Varnish Enterprise image for use with varnishncsa. This can be one of Always, Never, or IfNotPresent. Set this to "-" to inherit the value of `server.image.pullPolicy`.

tag.description: Sets the tag for the Varnish Enterprise image for use with varnishncsa. The Varnish image used here must be the same version as the Varnish Enterprise server. Set this to "-" to inherit the value of `server.image.tag`.

securityContext.description:
An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [securityContext][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container.

This securityContext will be set on the varnishncsa container. For setting securityContext on the Pod itself, see `global.podSecurityContext`. For setting securityContext to all containers, see `global.securityContext`.

extraArgs.description: Sets the extra arguments to varnishncsa.

extraEnvs.description: Sets additional environment variables for the varnishncsa container. Can be set as an object, an array of objects, or a template string.

startupProbe.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [startupProbe][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. The probe is disabled when empty. The probe command is set by the chart.

readinessProbe.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [readinessProbe][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. Set to `false` to disable the probe.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Sets the initial delay before the first probe is sent to determine if the varnishncsa Pod is ready to handle the logs.

periodSeconds.description: Sets the delay between each probe to determine if the varnishncsa Pod is ready to handle the logs after the initial probe.

timeoutSeconds.description: Sets the timeout for the probe to wait for a response from the varnishncsa Pod.

successThreshold.description: Sets the number of times when a consecutive successful response is considered a success and the varnishncsa Pod is considered ready to handle the logs.

failureThreshold.description: Sets the number of times when a consecutive failure response is considered a failure and the varnishncsa Pod is considered unhealthy.

livenessProbe.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [livenessProbe][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. Set to `false` to disable the probe.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Sets the initial delay before the first probe is sent to determine if the varnishncsa Pod is still ready to handle the logs.

periodSeconds.description: Sets the delay between each probe to determine if the varnishncsa Pod is still ready to handle the logs after the initial probe.

timeoutSeconds.description: Sets the timeout for the probe to wait for a response from the varnishncsa Pod.

successThreshold.description: Sets the number of times when a consecutive successful response is considered a success and the varnishncsa Pod is considered still ready to handle the logs.

failureThreshold.description: Sets the number of times when a consecutive failure response is considered a failure and the varnishncsa Pod is considered unhealthy.

resources.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [resources][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. This configuration can be used to limit resources consumed by the varnishncsa container.

extraVolumeMounts.description: An array of objects that conforms to the Kubernetes [volumeMounts][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. This configuration is used to mount extra volumes defined in `server.extraVolumes` into the varnishncsa container. The value can be set as either an array of objects or a template string.

otel.description: An object for configuring the Varnish OTEL sidecar.

enabled.description: Runs `/usr/bin/varnish-otel` in a sidecar container to export Varnish logs and metrics to an OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) endpoint. `varnish-otel` is included in the official `varnish` image since 9.0.3.

image.description: Sets the image and tag to use to deploy the Varnish OTEL sidecar. Setting a field to "-" inherits it from `server.image`.

repository.description: Sets the image repository of the OTEL sidecar. The image must be the same Varnish version as the server. When set to "-", `server.image.repository` is used.

pullPolicy.description: Sets the [imagePullPolicy][k8s-pod-v1-containers] of the OTEL sidecar. When set to "-", `server.image.pullPolicy` is used.

tag.description: Sets the image tag of the OTEL sidecar. When set to "-", `server.image.tag` is used.

securityContext.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [securityContext][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. This securityContext will be set on the OTEL container. For setting securityContext on the Pod itself, see `global.podSecurityContext`. For setting securityContext to all containers, see `global.securityContext`.

resources.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [resources][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. This configuration can be used to limit resources consumed by the OTEL container.

env.description: Sets environment variables of the OTEL container, typically to configure the OpenTelemetry exporters. See also the [OpenTelemetry environment variables specification](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/configuration/sdk-environment-variables/). Can be set as an object, an array of objects, or a template string.

initAgent.description: Configures the init container for Varnish Controller Agent.

enabled.description:
Configures whether to use init container to initialize Varnish Controller Agent state directory symbolic link. This is to allow Varnish Enterprise Pod to have a static path for accessing Varnish Controller Agent state files. When `server.initAgent.enabled` is `false`, the Varnish Controller Agent state directory will be discovered using a dynamic environment variable based on Pod name.

Before v1.6.0, the state directory symbolic link is created at `/etc/varnish/agent`.

From v1.6.0, the state directory symbolic link is created at `/etc/varnish/shared/agent`.

From v1.8.0, the default will be changed to `false`.

securityContext.description:
An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [securityContext][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container.

This securityContext will be set on the Varnish Controller Agent's init container. For setting securityContext on the Pod itself, see `global.podSecurityContext`. For setting securityContext to all containers, see `global.securityContext`.

extraVolumeMounts.description: Declares the extra volumes to mount with Varnish Controller Agent init container. Can be set as either a YAML list or a template string.

resources.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [resources][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. This configuration can be used to limit resources consumed by the Varnish Controller Agent init container.

agent.description: Configures Varnish Controller Agent sidecar for integration with Varnish Controller.

enabled.description:
Enables the Varnish Controller Agent for integration with Varnish Controller.

If Varnish Controller is deployed in a different namespace than Varnish Enterprise, also set `global.natsServer.internal.namespace`.

If Varnish Controller is deployed outside the Kubernetes cluster, or is using an external NATS server not provided by Varnish Controller Helm Chart, set `global.natsServer.internal.enabled` to `false` and configures `global.natsServer.externalAddress`.

licenseSecret.description: Removed: use `server.licenseSecret`. Only null is accepted, so that values files written for older chart versions still work.

image.description: Sets the image and tag to use to deploy Varnish Controller Agent sidecar. The image should be the same version as varnish-controller.

repository.description: Sets the repository for Varnish Controller Agent image. The Varnish Controller image used here must be the same version as the Varnish Controller. Since this is a different image from Varnish Enterprise, using "-" is unsupported.

pullPolicy.description: Sets the [imagePullPolicy][k8s-pod-v1-containers] for the Varnish Controller image. This can be one of Always, Never, or IfNotPresent.

tag.description: Sets the tag for the Varnish Controller image. The Varnish Controller image used here must be the same version as the Varnish Controller. Since this is a different image from Varnish Enterprise, using "-" is unsupported.

securityContext.description:
An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [securityContext][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container.

This securityContext will be set on the Varnish Controller container. For setting securityContext on the Pod itself, see `global.podSecurityContext`. For setting securityContext to all containers, see `global.securityContext`.

logLevel.description: Sets the log level for the Varnish Controller Agent. The value can be one of `debug`, `info`, `warning`, `error`, or `quiet`.

privateToken.description: Sets a Varnish Controller private token.

extraEnvs.description: Sets the extra environment variables for Varnish Controller Agent. Can be set as either an object, an array of objects, or a template string.

extraArgs.description: Sets the extra configuration args for Varnish Controller Agent.

tags.description: Sets the tags for the Varnish Controller Agent.

location.description:
Sets the location for this Varnish Controller Agent instance for use within Varnish Controller Router.

The location object can contain `latitude` and `longitude` keys to specify the geographic location of the server.

latitude.description: The latitude of the server, as a string.

longitude.description: The longitude of the server, as a string.

resources.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [resources][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. This configuration can be used to limit resources consumed by the Varnish Controller Agent container.

extraVolumeMounts.description: Declares the extra volumes to mount with Varnish Controller Agent container. Can be set as either a YAML list or a template string.

useReleaseName.description: When `server.replicas` is set to 1, use Helm Chart release name as Varnish Enterprise server name.

persistence.description: Configures persistence for Varnish Controller Agent state using PersistentVolumes. This configuration is only available when `server.kind` is set to StatefulSet. See the [Integration with Varnish Controller Agent](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-helm/guides/setting-up-varnish-controller-agent/) documentation for more information.

enabled.description: Enables Varnish Controller Agent state persistency using PersistentVolumes.

enableWithVolumeName.description: Enables Varnish Controller Agent state persistency using a custom volume mounts. This configuration overrides `server.agent.persistence.enabled`.

labels.description: Sets the extra labels for the PersistentVolumeClaim for Varnish Controller Agent. Can be set as an object or a template string.

annotations.description: Sets the extra annotations for the PersistentVolumeClaim for Varnish Controller Agent. Can be set as an object or a template string.

accessModes.description: Sets the storage access modes for the PersistentVolumeClaim for Varnish Controller Agent.

storageClassName.description: Sets the storage class for the PersistentVolumeClaim for Varnish Controller Agent.

storageSize.description: Sets the storage size for the PersistentVolumeClaim for Varnish Controller Agent.

autoRemove.description: Enables auto-removal of Varnish Enterprise instance with Varnish Controller upon pod rollout (e.g. during a redeployment).

method.description: Enable automatic de-registering of Varnish Controller Agent during Pod rollout. The value can be one of `none` (disabled), or `vcli` (use VCLI to perform de-registration).

image.description: Sets the image and tag to use to deploy Varnish Controller VCLI sidecar. The image should be the same version as varnish-controller.

repository.description: Sets the repository for the Varnish Controller VCLI image.

pullPolicy.description: Sets the [imagePullPolicy][k8s-pod-v1-containers] for the Varnish Controller VCLI image.

tag.description: Sets the tag for the Varnish Controller VCLI image.

securityContext.description:
An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [securityContext][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container.

This securityContext will be set on the Varnish Controller VCLI container. For setting securityContext on the Pod itself, see `global.podSecurityContext`. For setting securityContext to all containers, see `global.securityContext`.

externalAddress.description: Configures Varnish Controller Agent to use external Varnish Controller endpoint. Ignored if `server.agent.autoRemove.vcli.internal.enabled` is set to `true`.

username.description: Configures the username to connect to Varnish Controller API.

password.description: Configures NATS password as a string.

passwordFrom.description: Configures NATS password from a Kubernetes secret. By default, it uses an auto-generated password from a "varnish-controller-credentials" secret.

name.description: The name of the secret holding the password.

key.description: The key of the secret holding the password.

insecure.description: Configures Varnish Controller CLI container to skip verifying the certificate when communicating via HTTPS. This should be set to true if Varnish Controller is running with a self-signed certificates.

internal.description: Configures internal settings for Varnish Controller CLI container.

enabled.description: Configures Varnish Controller CLI container to use an internal Varnish Controller endpoint.

namespace.description: Configures the namespace Varnish Controller is deployed to. If left blank, the current namespace is used.

releaseName.description: Configures the release name Varnish Controller is deployed to. Use "varnish-controller" if left blank.

port.description: Configures the port of the Varnish Controller APIGW.

https.description: Configures Varnish Controller CLI container to use HTTPS instead of HTTP to communicate with the in-cluster Varnish Controller instance.

clusterDomain.description: Configures the NATS internal cluster domain name. Only change if NATS is deployed on a separate cluster.

resources.description: An object that conforms to the Kubernetes [resources][k8s-pod-v1-containers] definition of a Container. This configuration can be used to limit resources consumed by the Varnish Controller VCLI container.

extraEnvs.description: Sets the extra environment variables for Varnish Controller VCLI. Can be set as either an object, an array of objects, or a template string.

extraVolumeMounts.description: Declares the extra volumes to mount with Varnish Controller VCLI. Can be set as either a YAML list or a template string.

extraManifests.description: An array of objects to attach Kubernetes manifests to the workload.

name.description: The name of the manifest. Only used if `extraManifests[].checksum` is `true`.

checksum.description: Whether to attach the manifest's checksum to that of the workload in order to force an automatic rollout when the manifest is updated.

data.description: The full content of the manifest.

examples.name: clusterrole
examples.data:
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-clusterrole
# ...

cluster.description: An object for configuring clustering of the Varnish Enterprise Pods.

enabled.description:
Enables clustering and allows pods to shard requests between each others by:
- creating a headless service, even if `server.service.clusterIP != None`
- creating a secret token for pod to authorize peer-to-peer communication
- injecting a VCL preamble to your configuration

headlessServiceName.description: Configures the headless service used by pods to discover each others. If empty, the name defaults to `$VARNISH_SERVICE-peers` and the service is automatically created.

secretName.description: Configures the [token](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-enterprise/features/cluster/#token) used by nodes to authorize peer-to-peer communication. If empty, a `$VARNISH_SERVICE-cluster-secret` secret is automatically created.

primaries.description: Sets the number of [primaries](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-enterprise/features/cluster/#primaries) for each object. Must be a strictly positive integer. If unset, the Varnish Enterprise default is used.

fallback.description: Sets the [fallback](https://docs.varnish-software.com/varnish-enterprise/features/cluster/#fallback) level. Must be a positive integer (zero included). If unset, the Varnish Enterprise default is used.
